title: Introduce callchain-minimap compact trace overview and per-token attribution probe
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: Long, high-cardinality traces make it hard for oncall and SREs to get a quick signal about whether an invocation is a broad systemic issue or a localized expensive callsite. Existing dashboards surface per-route aggregates, but they lack a compact, at-a-glance representation that highlights hot callsites and per-token cost concentration across a single invocation. This PR introduces the 'callchain-minimap' concept: a compact, single-line visual summary for an invocation plus a lightweight backend compactor that produces per-invocation rollups suitable for dashboard sparklines and drilldown.

What this change contains: backend - a dedicated small service (trace-compactor) that subscribes to sampled trace events, builds a compact callchain digest, computes a minimap score (weighted by token-cost and latency), and emits two new metrics (invocation_minimap_score and invocation_compact_digest_id) along with optional sampled log anchors. The compactor uses a reservoir sampler keyed by tenant+route with token-cost and latency weighting to prioritise expensive/slow invocations. UI - a new React component CallchainMinimap that renders a compact SVG timeline and per-phase token-cost sparklines with hover tooltips and a one-click 'open-full-trace' action. Dashboard - a templated panel (Grafana/Chronicle compatible) that shows a sortable list of recent minimap rows for a route, with top-k token contributors.

Compatibility and opt-in: The compactor is behind a runtime feature-flag (telemetry.compactor.enabled=false by default). For Hosted tenants, the feature is off until a rollout window; Dedicated customers can enable via cluster-config. No existing trace schema is mutated; the compactor consumes existing spans and emits derived metrics.

Operational notes: compactor instances are horizontally scalable and memory-bounded (configurable reservoir size, default 1024 per shard). Emitted compact digests are stored in a small Redis-backed cache with 24h TTL by default; the dashboard fetches expanded context on demand to keep storage costs low. Alerts were tuned: a new alert rule minimap_high_entropy_trigger will fire only when minimap_score exceeds 0.85 and the token-cost concentration (top-3 tokens) exceeds 70% for more than 3m to reduce noise.

Why this is different: Instead of shipping heavier sampling or full trace persistence increases, this change introduces a compact, attribution-first signal that surfaces likely root causes quickly and directs engineers to full trace when necessary. It targets the long-tail investigative workflow: rapid scannability, low storage cost, and per-token explainability.

Checklist:
- [x] Backend service and deployment manifests
- [x] Metrics and registry entries
- [x] UI component and dashboard panel template
- [x] Unit and e2e tests for compactor and UI
- [x] Documentation and runbook entry

Related: ENG-6721 (compactor design), ENG-6882 (dashboard UX), PM-421 (product signal prioritization).

review_comments: Marcus Nguyen: Nice idea — can we make the reservoir sampler deterministic per shard to improve reproducibility during incident replay?
Sofia Patel: Responded that sampler now seeds with shard id + epoch; added unit test to assert deterministic ordering under same inputs.
Elena Gomez: The minimap_score threshold seems aggressive; worried about alert noise at 0.6 for busy tenants.
Sofia Patel: Tuned alert to require both minimap_score > 0.85 and token concentration > 70% for 3m; added smoke tests for the rule.
Ravi Kapoor: backend Redis cache TTL should be configurable via ENV; also request that we emit a telemetry tag for compactor_version.
Sofia Patel: Added REDIS_TTL config and compactor_version tag; updated deployment manifest and docs.
Marcus Nguyen: CI flake on e2e fixed in follow-up commit; approving change.
Elena Gomez: LGTM — approving after small docs nits fixed.
release_notes: Add compact 'callchain-minimap' trace summary and per-invocation token attribution probe. Opt-in via feature flag; improves triage and reduces full-trace noise for long-tail invocations.
